brief: A system monitor where CPU/memory are organisms — healthy breathes steady, stressed pulses fast

dominant_strengths: Clean dark dashboard palette with disciplined cyan/green hierarchy that reads instantly as healthy telemetry data.
Solid typographic scale separating labels, values, and percentages with adequate contrast and consistent uppercase metadata.
dominant_weaknesses: The 'organism' metaphor is barely realized — static gradient spheres and rings show no breath, pulse, or stress deformation.
Two giant identical orbs dominate while real metrics (temp, swap, load) are demoted to tiny footer text, inverting information priority.
Visual language is generic sci-fi dashboard; nothing communicates 'living thing' versus a standard radial gauge.
fix_priorities: Animate the spheres: slow sinusoidal scale at low load, rapid jittery pulses and color shift toward amber/red as utilization climbs.
Differentiate the two organisms morphologically — shape, texture, or rhythm — so CPU and Memory feel like distinct creatures, not twins.
Promote secondary stats into the orb's silhouette (rings as cores, satellites as processes) instead of footer key-value pairs.
Introduce a stress state visual vocabulary (tremor, distortion, halo) so the brief's healthy-vs-stressed dichotomy is legible at a glance.
rationale.norman_balance: Visceral is moderate from the glowing orbs, behavioral is weak because key data is buried, and reflective is low since the organism concept never lands.
rationale.intent_fit: Only superficially — it looks like cells but lacks any motion or stress semantics that would make CPU/memory feel like living organisms.
